dataset: UAE Insurance Ecosystem Explorer — Evidence Register v1
scope: Initial evidence layer for UAE market-level insurance intelligence. This is not a complete census, legal opinion, or validated opportunity assessment.

classification_legend.FACT: Directly stated in the cited primary source; limited to that source's scope and period.
classification_legend.ANALYSIS: Interpretation derived from one or more facts; not itself a source fact.
classification_legend.HYPOTHESIS: Research question or opportunity proposition that requires validation.
classification_legend.VERIFICATION_REQUIRED: A primary source exists or is identified, but its current detail, completeness, applicability, or data extraction has not yet been checked.

source_registry.title: Quarterly Economic Review — March 2026, section III.3 Insurance Developments
source_registry.status: primary source located; figures cross-checked against 2025 Annual Report
source_registry.limitations: The QER's narrative refers to Q4 2025 while key annual figures reflect full-year 2025; retain the table/period labels when citing individual values.

source_registry.title: CBUAE Annual Report 2025
source_registry.limitations: Use the report table and definition for every extracted metric; avoid mixing annual and quarterly values.

source_registry.title: CBUAE Licensing — Register of Insurance Entities, Entity List of 2026
source_registry.status: official register page located; underlying downloadable list not yet extracted into a normalized entity census
source_registry.limitations: A current count in a quarterly report is not a substitute for entity-by-entity licence status. Record legal name, entity type, licence/registration, status, jurisdiction and checked date when extracting.

source_registry.title: Health Insurance Providers Permit Services
source_registry.source_type: official emirate health-insurance permit register/service page
source_registry.status: official page located; individual list entries require extraction
source_registry.limitations: A DHA health insurance permit is not the same thing as a federal insurance licence. Distinguish insurer, broker, TPA and provider permissions.

source_registry.publisher: Department of Health — Abu Dhabi (document originally issued by HAAD)
source_registry.title: Health Insurance Claims Adjudication Standard, HSF/CA/1.0
source_registry.period: Issue date December 2010; current applicability requires confirmation
source_registry.status: primary document located; version/current applicability not yet confirmed
source_registry.limitations: Do not treat the 2010 version as the complete current ruleset until DOH confirms superseding standards, circulars and current claims rules.

source_registry.title: Standard for the Principles and Procedures Governing the Recovery of Payment for Healthcare Services under the Health Insurance Scheme
source_registry.period: Current applicability to be checked against latest DOH standards/circulars
source_registry.limitations: Scope includes payers, TPAs, providers and recovery processes; read with linked current documents, not in isolation.

source_registry.title: Electronic Claims Audit Orientation — Health Insurance, Circular CIR-2026-00000162
source_registry.limitations: This is an orientation notice highlighting documentation completeness, updated records and correct medical coding; it is not a complete claims adjudication rulebook.

evidence_records.claim: CBUAE's 2025 Annual Report reports UAE gross written premiums of AED 75.2 billion in 2025, versus AED 65.1 billion in 2024.
evidence_records.source_location: Annual Report 2025, Key Financial Data / Gross Written Premiums; QER March 2026, Insurance Developments
evidence_records.use_limit: Market-wide aggregate; does not by itself prove demand or profitability in any specific product line.

evidence_records.claim: CBUAE's 2025 Annual Report reports gross paid claims of AED 46.2 billion in 2025, versus AED 41.6 billion in 2024.
evidence_records.source_location: Annual Report 2025, Key Financial Data / Gross Paid Claims
evidence_records.use_limit: Aggregate gross paid claims; not a measure of rejected claims, claim-processing cost, or avoidable leakage.

evidence_records.claim: CBUAE's March 2026 Quarterly Economic Review reports 58 licensed insurance companies in Q4 2025: 22 traditional national companies, 10 national takaful companies and 26 branches of foreign insurance companies.
evidence_records.source_location: Section III.3, Insurance Sector Structure and Activity
evidence_records.use_limit: Do not present this as a live 2026 entity-by-entity licence census; verify the CBUAE Entity List of 2026 for current status.

evidence_records.claim: CBUAE's March 2026 Quarterly Economic Review reports 2025 health insurance gross written premiums of AED 35.5 billion and health gross paid claims of AED 27.4 billion.
evidence_records.source_location: Section III.3, Key Performance Indicators; insurance line breakdown
evidence_records.period: FY2025 as reported in the review
evidence_records.status: source-backed; confirm exact table footnotes before reusing in charts
evidence_records.use_limit: Premium and paid-claim aggregates are not directly comparable as a loss ratio without aligning earned premium, incurred claims, reserves, reinsurance and reporting definitions.

evidence_records.claim: CBUAE provides an official licensing page identifying a 2026 Entity List for insurance entities.
evidence_records.source_location: CBUAE Licensing page, CBUAE Register Insurance Entities
evidence_records.status: register entry point verified; entity-level extraction pending
evidence_records.use_limit: Do not claim a complete named list or infer an entity's current status until the downloadable register is extracted and each record checked.

evidence_records.claim: DHA describes its health-insurance permit service as covering permits for insurance companies, brokers, TPAs and healthcare providers; a DHA Health Insurance Permit authorises an insurance company to sell health products within Dubai.
evidence_records.use_limit: Dubai permit scope must not be confused with CBUAE federal licensing or other emirate requirements.

evidence_records.claim: The located Abu Dhabi Health Insurance Claims Adjudication Standard describes adjudication as determining payer financial responsibility after applying member benefits and distinguishes simple edits from complex edits.
evidence_records.period: Document issue date December 2010; current applicability pending
evidence_records.status: document content identified; current version not verified
evidence_records.use_limit: Use as a historical/located standard until current DOH status and amendments are verified.

evidence_records.claim: The located DOH standard on recovery of healthcare-service payments says it covers recovery reasons, process and payer/provider obligations and should be read alongside claims adjudication, medical billing and other DOH documents.
evidence_records.status: document content identified; current version not verified
evidence_records.use_limit: Do not treat the standard as a complete standalone claims rule set.

evidence_records.claim: DHA's September 2026 electronic claims audit orientation highlights keeping documents and reports complete/current and using correct medical coding when submitting electronic claims.
evidence_records.source_location: Circular CIR-2026-00000162, purpose and important note
evidence_records.use_limit: Operational orientation only; not a substitute for the applicable DHA claims standards, circulars, data standards or payer contract.

evidence_records.claim: Health insurance is a priority for deeper claims-operations research because the official report gives both premium and paid-claim aggregates and separate emirate-level claims/permit sources are identifiable.
evidence_records.status: analytical prioritisation, not a confirmed commercial opportunity
evidence_records.use_limit: Test against actual workflow volumes, buyer pain, operational budgets and current rule applicability.

evidence_records.claim: A source-linked claims-quality checklist or human-reviewed audit-support workflow may help providers or claims teams reduce missing-document and coding-related rework.
evidence_records.use_limit: No quantified savings, demand, willingness to pay or compliance effect has been established.

sector_research_links.analysis: The strongest current evidence coverage in this initial batch: market aggregates, a located Abu Dhabi adjudication standard and a recent DHA claims-audit notice.
